audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill, Skill, Riven, Riven while the packet chart over 4283 games reads Skill, Nautilus, Nautilus, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven - the two early stages he owns are given to Riven, and the two she owns are given away as coinflips.
audit.why: The page's own whys already describe the packet chart: whys[1] calls Level 2 'his strongest relative window', whys[2] says a hooked Riven cannot land Ki Burst and he has 'full control of trades', whys[3] says the short trade at 4-5 is 'decisively' Riven's, and whys[4] says Level 6 is a reliable kill. Only the tokens disagreed with the prose. The nautilus__riven mirror flipped rows 1-4 to exactly these values as one atomic group.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 and 2 to Nautilus, rows 3 and 4 to Riven, in both layers as one atomic paired group, ratings moved with them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line's cooldown is written as 15 seconds in two places, and Titan's Wrath is never mentioned at any stage.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10s, not a flat 15 - and the drop to 10 by rank 5 is exactly why the safe window shrinks as the lane goes on. Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield that turns his autos into a damage-over-time aura, so it is the thing that decides whether an extended trade is worth taking; a full Riven rotation outlasts it.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into whys[1], whys[3], the Level 2 spike and the mid-game prose, with Titan's Wrath named.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riven's abilities are unnamed throughout the content layer - 'Q dash chain', 'W stun', 'E sideways' - and Nautilus's are half-named, with Riptide called 'his E AOE' and Staggering Blow called 'his passive root'.
audit.why: Both kits have real names in Riot's data: Broken Wings, Ki Burst, Valor, Blade of the Exile against Staggering Blow, Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath, Riptide, Depth Charge. The decisive numbers are Ki Burst's 11s at rank 1 against Dredge Line's 14s, which is what makes the step-up window real, and Broken Wings' three dashes on one 13s cooldown plus Valor as a fourth - the reason he must never throw the hook on cooldown. The nautilus__riven mirror states the same pairing.
audit.corrected: Real names and both cooldowns written through whys[1], whys[2], whys[3], both early spikes, the early and mid prose and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says what happens when Dredge Line misses you and hits terrain instead.
audit.why: Dredge Line carries the terrain flag: colliding with terrain pulls Nautilus toward it. Against a Riven who sidesteps toward a wall, a whiffed hook is not simply a whiffed hook - it can still close the gap, so 'dodge it and step in' is only safe when there is no wall behind you.

edits.before: His Dredge Line comes online at level 2 and a landed hook cancels your Q-dash animation mid-chain — his CC advantage makes this stage his strongest relative window.
edits.after: Dredge Line lands at level 2 on a 14-second cooldown and a hook cancels your Broken Wings dash mid-chain — his CC density makes this his strongest window of the lane.

edits.before: Hook into passive root into E AOE is a three-stage lockdown chain he can assemble in under two seconds — a hooked Riven cannot land W or complete a combo, giving him full control of trades.
edits.after: Dredge Line into Staggering Blow into Riptide is a three-stage lockdown he assembles in under two seconds — a hooked Riven never lands Ki Burst, so he controls every trade in this window.

edits.before: With all three basic abilities available and Dredge Line on a 15-second cooldown you have a wide enough gap after each miss to E-dodge, W-stun him before his passive restacks, and win the short trade decisively.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 against Ki Burst's 11s, so every miss opens a gap that belongs to you — Valor sideways past the hook, Ki Burst before Staggering Blow restacks, and the short trade is decisively yours.

edits.before: Nautilus unlocks his Q hook at level 2 — one landed Dredge Line interrupts your Q dash chain mid-animation and chains into his passive root, negating your entire combo.
edits.after: Dredge Line unlocks at level 2 on 14s — one hook cancels Broken Wings mid-dash into Staggering Blow, and a miss into terrain still drags him to you, so never sidestep toward a wall.

edits.before: His Q hook into passive-root into E AOE chains his CC so tightly that a hooked Riven at half health cannot fight back — dodge Dredge Line at all costs in this window.
edits.after: Dredge Line into Staggering Blow into Riptide, itself only 5-7s, chains so tightly that a hooked Riven at half health cannot fight back — dodge the hook at all costs here.

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely neutral — Nautilus has no dash, no hook yet, and his autos are painfully slow, but you only have Q poke without your W stun to confirm a real trade. Farm with the first hit of Broken Wings and stay out of auto range so his passive root proc does not surprise you. The moment he hits level 2 and unlocks Dredge Line the dynamic flips hard: a landed hook mid-Q-chain cancels your dash animation entirely, chains into his passive root, and gives him free auto-root procs plus his E AOE — that sequence will delete a third of your health bar for almost zero input from you. Respect the hook range visually and E sideways on any cast animation you see from him.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely neutral — Nautilus has no dash, no hook yet, and his autos are painfully slow, but you only have Broken Wings without Ki Burst to confirm a real trade. Farm with the first cast and stay out of auto range so Staggering Blow does not root you for free. The moment he hits level 2 and unlocks Dredge Line the dynamic flips hard: a hook mid-chain cancels your dash outright, chains into Staggering Blow, and buys him free auto roots plus Riptide — that sequence takes a third of your health bar for almost no input from you. Dredge Line reaches 1150 units, so respect that range and Valor sideways on any cast you read.

edits.before: Your level 3 full chain is normally the window where you punish immobile melee tanks, but Nautilus's CC density keeps this matchup even well into levels 4-5. The pattern to exploit is his 15-second Q cooldown: the instant Dredge Line misses or you E-dodge it, you have a clean window with no hook threat — that is your cue to Q dash onto him, W-stun before his passive root stacks again, and rip through the full rotation. At level 6 the equation shifts decisively in your favour; Blade of the Exile's extended range means you can land the last Q-chain hit and Wind Slash execute before he can disengage, and his lack of mobility means he cannot escape the execute cone once the all-in is committed.
edits.after: Your level 3 chain is normally where you punish immobile melee tanks, but Nautilus's CC density holds him ahead until levels 4-5. The pattern to exploit is Dredge Line's cooldown: 14 seconds at rank 1, falling to 10 by rank 5. The instant it misses or you Valor past it, there is no hook threat — Broken Wings onto him, Ki Burst before Staggering Blow restacks, then rip the rotation. Titan's Wrath is only a 12-second shield, so a full rotation outlasts it. At level 6 the equation shifts decisively your way: Blade of the Exile's extra range lands the last Broken Wings hit and Wind Slash before he disengages, and with no dash he cannot leave once you commit.

edits.before: Stack his passive auto-roots and E AOE slow to prevent you landing a clean W stun
edits.after: Stack Staggering Blow roots and layer Riptide slows so you never land a clean Ki Burst

edits.before: E-dash to dodge his Dredge Line hook before committing your Q chain
edits.after: Valor sideways to dodge Dredge Line before committing Broken Wings

notes: Packet suspectName 'His Dredge Line' is a FALSE POSITIVE - the correct ability name with a possessive pronoun in front of it. Chart rows 1-4 proposed as one atomic paired group across both layers to match the 4283-game packet chart, the page's own whys and the nautilus__riven mirror. Not asserted anywhere, because Riot's text does not cover it: whether Depth Charge's travelling shockwave can be outrun by Broken Wings or Valor, and whether Riven's dashes can carry her out of a landed Dredge Line pull. Both are left out rather than guessed - see questionsForUser.
